solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flirt with casual girl around the end of December

parts.note: a casual worker is a temp, someone hired short-term

indicators.note: the girl's name goes around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of December

explanation.surface: A man takes up with a girl he met casually over the Christmas season.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirt, used as a noun, is a woman who leads men on, which is what a seductress does.

clue.text: Plump for bath alongside

parts.note: a bath is a tub
by means beside or alongside

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a bath that sits next to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' looks like a phrase meaning choose; here 'Plump' alone is the definition and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is rather fat and rounded.

clue.text: Travelling with unfortunately grim worker

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters of grim are put out of order

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone on the move alongside a gloomy labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges GRIM to MIGR.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrant as an adjective describes people or birds that move from place to place, so it means travelling.

clue.text: Small drinks container priests take in time

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: the priests take the time letter inside them

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest, so priests are cures

explanation.surface: Priests pour themselves little drinks from a container in their own time.
explanation.walkthrough: CURES with T taken in becomes CTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is jokingly a small alcoholic drink, from its sense of a medicine dissolved in alcohol.

clue.text: Sat uncomfortably in delicate pants, like Teddy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of Sat go inside the rearranged letters of delicate
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word delicate is made a mess of
sitting uncomfortably means shifting about, so the letters of Sat are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone sat squirming in flimsy underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncomfortably' makes AST, 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) makes ELICATED. A teddy here is a woman's one-piece undergarment, not the bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a one-piece undergarment, typically made with stretchy elastic sections.

clue.text: Saskatchewan music

indicators.note: read loosely as music to be found in the province, pointing to letters sitting inside its name; the setter gives no clearer signal

parts.note: the Canadian prairie province, whose name holds the answer at letters three to five

explanation.surface: A label for music from a Canadian prairie province.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals that the answer is concealed in the province's name; the clue has to be read as 'the music in Saskatchewan'. Ska is a Jamaican style of the late 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican genre of popular music, a forerunner of reggae, and its letters sit inside the province's name.

clue.text: Gets ready for hols with lots of Scouts

definitions.meaning: puts clothes into a suitcase before a holiday
Cub Scouts are organised in groups each called a pack

explanation.surface: A troop of Scouts getting ready to go away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack is to fill a case for travel; a pack is also a group of Cubs or Brownies.

clue.text: Ordinary level described

indicators.note: a description is spoken, so the word for level is given as it sounds

parts.note: a plane is a flat, level surface

explanation.surface: An ordinary-grade qualification being explained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' is a loose sound signal: PLANE (level) sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple, unremarkable and everyday.

clue.text: Cheshire town loses last share; that's style!

indicators.note: the town's name drops its final letter

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in the English county of Cheshire
a cut is a share of the takings

explanation.surface: A Cheshire town forfeits its final share, and someone shrugs that this is the way of things.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England; without its last letter it is CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a hairstyle, cut very short all over.

clue.text: Sell Amber deviously; just a half maybe?

indicators.note: acting deviously means not straight, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A barman sells amber ale on the sly, perhaps only by the half-pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' rearranges SELL AMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer means something trivial, and literally weak beer; a half-pint is a modest drink, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Away with you, nearly up-ending best plant

indicators.note: nearly means short of the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: begone is an old command telling someone to leave

indicators.note: to up-end is to turn upside down, so the letters for best are turned round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone shoos away a prize plant, nearly upending it.
explanation.walkthrough: BEGONE nearly is BEGON; 'up-ending' turns AI into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a flowering garden and house plant.

clue.text: Unnerved, run off to East 2nd Avenue

indicators.note: the run letter goes off, removed from the word

parts.note: unnerved means alarmed
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the second letter of the word East is taken

explanation.surface: A nervous runner sets off for East Second Avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: ALARMED without R gives ALAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined public walk or avenue, from Spanish.

clue.text: It gives rise to unusually easy time

indicators.note: doing something unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters of easy are reordered

explanation.surface: Something brings about a rare stretch of leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges EASY to YEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the leavening agent that makes bread dough rise.

clue.text: Scientific reappraisal of clan ethic

indicators.note: a reappraisal looks at something again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A scientific review of a clan's moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reappraisal of' rearranges CLAN ETHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical describes matters of applied science and engineering.

clue.text: Is at odds with undertakings I'd backed into

indicators.note: the reversed letters go into the word for undertakings

parts.note: contracts are formal undertakings

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the two letters run the other way

parts.note: I'd written without its apostrophe gives two letters

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the commitments they personally reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' makes DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict is to disagree with or be inconsistent with something.

clue.text: Rubbish computers keep concealed in retribution

indicators.note: the letters for computers and keep are hidden inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: tat is cheap, shoddy rubbish
IT, information technology, stands for computers
a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort

explanation.surface: Revenge on a hoarder: junk computers locked away out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' looks like a verb with 'concealed'; it is the castle stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, paying someone back blow for blow.

clue.text: Best illustrator, best quality

parts.note: top means best
an illustrator is someone who draws, a drawer

explanation.surface: A prize-winning artist of the highest calibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest class or finest kind.

clue.text: Swindler to enter Rio clandestinely to explore

indicators.note: done clandestinely means in disguise, so these letters are disguised by rearrangement

parts.note: a con man, or con, is a swindler

explanation.surface: A conman slips secretly into Rio to scout the territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clandestinely' rearranges CON with ENTER and RIO, all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconnoitre is to survey or explore an area to gather information.

clue.text: Ask too much for retrospective test to be abandoned anew

indicators.note: the letters of test are given up from the longer word
the remaining letters are arranged anew into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A retrospective exam is to be scrapped and started again.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, E, S, T from RETROSPECTIVE ('to be abandoned') and rearrange what is left ('anew').
explanation.definitionFit: To overprice is to set a price higher than something is worth.

clue.text: In US state capital, partner gets prime site for temporary homes

indicators.note: the partner and letter go in the capital's name

parts.note: Pierre is the capital of South Dakota

indicators.note: the partner gets the letter inside

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner

indicators.note: the prime, or first, letter of site

explanation.surface: In an American capital, a business partner secures a top location for short-stay housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' makes DSATE; Pierre is the capital of South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small flat kept for occasional stays, a second base rather than a main residence.

clue.text: Sculptor on record as having large mug!

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: An artist on a record is shown with a big face.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug also means face, so 'large mug' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: See 14 across
Diet at lunchtime is a con!

parts.note: to diet severely is to fast
lunchtime is one o'clock

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a midday diet is a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a fast one is a trick or deception, a swindle.

clue.text: Returned to small lake surrounded by grass

indicators.note: the small letter and lake go inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a pond is a small lake

explanation.surface: Someone went back to a little lake ringed with grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' suggests going back, but here it means replied.
explanation.definitionFit: Responded means answered, as in returning a reply.

clue.text: How to log your content with the science?

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what lies within its letters

explanation.surface: A query about how to record your findings in scientific work.
explanation.definitionFit: An ology is a jocular word for any branch of science or study.

clue.text: Arrogant sort turns up to bowl

indicators.note: turns means flips round, so the word up runs the other way

parts.note: to shy is to throw or bowl

explanation.surface: A conceited type shows up to bowl at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: UP turned is PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushy describes someone overbearing and self-assertive.

clue.text: Blimey, agreement holds central bookings back

indicators.note: the word of agreement holds the pair inside

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

indicators.note: back means the pair is reversed
the central letters of bookings are its middle pair

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation as a deal turns on the core reservations being reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' picks the middle pair of bookings; 'back' turns them round to make IK.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of shock or surprise.

clue.text: Put to one side an anagram for dandelion?

parts.note: a dandelion is a common weed
out is a standard crossword signal for an anagram

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's whimsy: words for discarding something, posed as a wordplay question about a garden weed.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer, read as crossword wordplay, would itself instruct a solver to jumble a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed out is to remove or set aside the unwanted members of a group.

clue.text: See 14 across
Wind gauge in crevice

indicators.note: the gauge goes in the crevice

parts.note: a chink is a narrow crack or crevice
OO is a model railway track gauge

explanation.surface: An instrument for measuring wind is wedged into a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: OO is the most common British model railway gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a warm, dry wind descending the eastern Rockies.

clue.text: Long-legged veteran gymnast admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the answer is held within the phrase

explanation.surface: A seasoned gymnast with long limbs is accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes a tall, slim person or animal with long limbs.

clue.text: Tawdry and bland

definitions.meaning: showy and cheap, lacking good taste

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both vulgar in style and without flavour.
